checks.claim: Mount Fuji is a stratovolcano 3,776 meters tall
checks.why: NASA and UNESCO both give 3,776 m and call it a stratovolcano.

sources.title: Mount Fuji, Japan - NASA Earth Observatory

checks.claim: Stratovolcanoes are built of alternating layers of lava flows and ash
checks.why: USGS CVO describes them exactly so; NPS notes the layers are not always orderly, which does not change the claim.

checks.claim: Gas dissolved in magma expands as it rises and drives explosive eruptions
checks.why: USGS sources say gas comes out of solution as pressure drops and the expanding gas powers explosive eruptions.

sources.title: Volcanic gases create air pollution on the Island of Hawai'i - USGS
